title.en: Identify spherical, cylindrical and plane wavefronts

say.en: Drop a stone in a pond and circles spread out. Huygens imagined that every point on a circle starts its own tiny ripple, and that explains how light travels. In this lesson: Define a wavefront.
Identify spherical, cylindrical and plane wavefronts.
State Huygens principle.

body.en: A wavefront is a surface on which the disturbance has the same phase at a given time. A point source gives spherical *wavefronts*, a linear source gives cylindrical ones, and far from any source a small part of the wavefront is plane. Rays are normal to the wavefronts, and the wavefront moves with the wave speed.
body.kn: ಒಂದೇ ಕಲೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಕಂಪಿಸುವ ಬಿಂದುಗಳ ಮೇಲ್ಮೈಯೇ ತರಂಗಮುಖ. ಬಿಂದು ಆಕರ: ಗೋಳೀಯ; ರೇಖಾ ಆಕರ: ಸಿಲಿಂಡರಾಕಾರ; ದೂರದಲ್ಲಿ: ಸಮತಲ. ಕಿರಣ ತರಂಗಮುಖಕ್ಕೆ ಲಂಬ.

say.en: A wavefront is a surface on which the disturbance has the same phase at a given time. A point source gives spherical wavefronts, a linear source gives cylindrical ones, and far from any source a small part of the wavefront is plane. Rays are normal to the wavefronts, and the wavefront moves with the wave speed. Point source gives spherical.
say.kn: ಒಂದೇ ಕಲೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಕಂಪಿಸುವ ಬಿಂದುಗಳ ಮೇಲ್ಮೈಯೇ ತರಂಗಮುಖ. ಬಿಂದು ಆಕರ: ಗೋಳೀಯ; ರೇಖಾ ಆಕರ: ಸಿಲಿಂಡರಾಕಾರ; ದೂರದಲ್ಲಿ: ಸಮತಲ. ಕಿರಣ ತರಂಗಮುಖಕ್ಕೆ ಲಂಬ.

say.en: Line source gives cylindrical.
Distant source gives plane.
Ray is perpendicular to wavefront.

narration.en: Let us draw wavefronts from near and far sources and then use Huygens' construction.

say.en: A point source sends out spherical wavefronts: surfaces where the wave has the same phase. Rays are perpendicular to them.
Far from the source, a small part of a huge sphere is almost flat: a plane wavefront with parallel rays.
Huygens: every point on a wavefront is a source of secondary wavelets. After time τ each wavelet has radius vτ.
The forward envelope of all the wavelets is the new wavefront A′B′.
In glass, light travels at 2 × 10⁸ m/s, so in one nanosecond the wavelets grow to 20 cm.
Let us draw wavefronts from near and far sources and then use Huygens' construction.

narration.en: Every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets that spread at the speed of the wave. After a time t each wavelet has radius vt, and the surface touching all of them in front, their envelope, is the new wavefront. A plane wavefront stays plane; a spherical one grows.

body.en: Each point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets that spread out with the speed of the wave. After a time $t$, the new wavefront is the forward envelope (common tangent) of all wavelets of radius $vt$. The backward wave is ignored.
body.kn: ತರಂಗಮುಖದ ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ಬಿಂದುವೂ ದ್ವಿತೀಯಕ ಅಲೆಗಳ ಆಕರ. t ಕಾಲದ ನಂತರ ಈ ಅಲೆಗಳ ಮುಂಭಾಗದ ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಸ್ಪರ್ಶಕವೇ ಹೊಸ ತರಂಗಮುಖ.

problem.en: A plane wavefront moves through water (n = 4/3). How far do the secondary wavelets spread in 1 ns?

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A plane wavefront moves through water (n = 4/3). How far do the secondary wavelets spread in 1 ns?

say.en: Let us solve this together. A plane wavefront moves through water (n equals 4 over 3). How far do the secondary wavelets spread in 1 ns?
v equals c over n equals 3 times 10 to the power 8 over (4 over 3) equals 2.25 times 10 to the power 8 metres per second.
Radius equals vt equals 2.25 times 10 to the power 8 times 10 to the power minus 9 equals 0.225 metres.
So the answer is 22.5 centimetres.
